identity_reason: a layout primitive only places other components and has no look of its own to derive
concept: Flex places parts along one line with a gap from the 4px step, and lets one part take the spare room, so a row of keys and a display share a unit face without any part changing its own size.

root.why: A flex box keeps its children in fixed positions along one line so a layout never reflows between states.

inline.why: An inline flex sits in a line of text without breaking it, so a label and its key keep one place on the line.

row.why: Parts sit side by side along one line, like the keys printed along the bottom of a case.

column.why: Parts stack top to bottom in DOM order, so the reading order and the visual order are the same.

wrap.why: A line that runs out of room breaks to a new line instead of shrinking a part below its own size.

g-xs.why: The smallest gap is one 4px step, the same pitch the grille holes sit on.

g-sm.why: A small gap of two steps separates a label from the part it names.

g-md.why: A medium gap of four steps separates neighbouring parts inside one unit face.

g-lg.why: A large gap of six steps separates one unit from the next so each reads as its own appliance.

g-xl.why: The section gap of eight steps separates groups of units, such as rooms on a home screen.

a-start.why: Start alignment keeps labels on the inset line where printing sits on a case.

a-center.why: Centre alignment puts the loud control in the clear area the hand expects to find it in.

a-end.why: End alignment places the lowercase model name on the bottom inset line.

a-stretch.why: Stretch lets a display window run the full inner size of the unit, aligned to the inset.

a-baseline.why: Baseline alignment sets printed labels of different sizes on one line, as type is set on a case.

j-start.why: Parts pack at the start of the line and stay put when a part is added or removed.

j-center.why: Parts packed in the middle put the loud control in the clear area of the unit.

j-end.why: Parts packed at the end put the loud control lower or right of the display, where the hand expects it.

j-between.why: The first part sits on one inset and the last on the other, so the ends of a line never move with the content.

item.why: A flex item holds its own size by default, so a part keeps the face it was made with.

grow.why: One part takes the spare room so a display window fills the line between two keys.

no-shrink.why: A key that must stay full size refuses to shrink, so its 44px target holds in a tight line.

s-start.why: One part can sit on the start inset line while the rest of the line is centred.

s-center.why: One part can sit in the middle of the line while the rest start on the inset.

s-end.why: One part can sit on the end inset line while the rest of the line starts.
